intent: Develop a readable tiger overturn using two control rods, with staged height difference and coordinated arcing

interpretations.in_screen_overturn: Head-to-rear vector rotates through near-vertical and the endpoints exchange left/right order
interpretations.axial_side_roll: Rotation about the head-to-rear line is not determined by two point positions alone; joint and attachment constraints require separate examination

established_local_directions.servo_7_and_9_common_increase: roughly Sony-right motion in prior local trials

conceptual_stages_after_measurement: Establish a visible height difference while observing body articulation and depth
Coordinate both endpoints around a shared moving centre without collapsing their separation
Inspect near-vertical configuration, rod crossing location and front/back layering before crossing it
Only after those stages are verified, exchange screen-left/right order and settle the tiger inverted

conceptual_geometry.note: A two-dimensional geometric guide only. Not a calibrated servo inverse map, rigid-body model, depth clearance certificate, or executable path. Articulated endpoint separation cannot be forced from a single image.

latest_height_sweep.finding: Visible head rise and body inclination, with no head/rear left-right exchange. Height difference alone did not demonstrate a turnover.
latest_height_sweep.next_measurement: Coordinated endpoint arcing and rod front/back separation remain unverified. No executable inversion target is inferred from this pitch sweep.
